reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about segregation-driven embrittlement in single-phase HEAs, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises. All claims rely on uncited assertions rather than demonstrated experimental or computational results.
premises: Minor element segregation at grain boundaries can occur in single-phase HEAs without bulk phase separation
Such segregation reduces intergranular cohesion and causes brittle behavior
This mechanism is distinct from conventional alloy embrittlement by coarse precipitates
Thermal aging or deformation can promote the necessary atomic mobility for segregation
The effect is measurable under service-like temperatures and loading rates
